rationale: Second pass: with the core map accepted (audit_spec_version 1), I investigated the recovery sub-case classifier and TryPreAccept path against the accepted map. The most concrete sourced discrepancy is that the defer-cycle guard in handleTryPreAcceptReply is inert: lb.possibleQuorum is initialized all-false and only ever assigned false (line 1445-1446), and the notInQuorum loop tests lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] using the constant reply's AcceptorId for every q (line 1461) instead of lb.possibleQuorum[q]. Consequently notInQuorum is always r.N and the comparison notInQuorum == r.N/2 cannot hold, so the block guarded by the in-source comment 'this is to prevent defer cycles' never executes. Two premises remain open before this is a defect: whether handlePrepareReply can even select sub-case 4 (its predicate is textually identical to sub-case 3, line 1305-1309, so the TryPreAccept exchange may be unreachable), and whether executeCommands otherwise retriggers recovery for a deferred instance. I also rechecked the handlePreAccept branch that writes InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][preAccept.Instance].Cmds: every path that sets an instance to ACCEPTED/COMMITTED also sets Cmds from the same bookkeeping, so I could not source a history producing Status>=ACCEPTED with Cmds==nil; I am not raising it as a defect and keep it as a local anomaly. No defect is claimed here.

feedback.answered: The TryPreAccept defer-cycle guard is inert in this implementation: possibleQuorum is never set true and the notInQuorum loop indexes a constant (tpar.AcceptorId), so notInQuorum == r.N/2 is unreachable and the guard block never runs. The handlePreAccept wrong-row write (InstanceSpace[LeaderId]) was investigated for reachability; no path was sourced that leaves an instance at Status>=ACCEPTED with Cmds==nil, so it is retained as a local anomaly rather than a candidate.
remaining: Whether handlePrepareReply can select recovery sub-case 4 at all (duplicate sub-case 3/4 predicate), which would determine whether the inert defer-cycle guard is merely dead code or a lost protection.
Whether a recovering coordinator that defers is retriggered by executeCommands, i.e. whether the missing guard can cause a permanent stall.
Whether the same duplicate-predicate deviation makes the direct-accept sub-case 3 fire too early, i.e. a safety question separate from the liveness guard.
Membership (A4) and thrifty/quorum-file selection remain unread; the fast/slow thresholds used in these predicates depend on them.
feedback.rationale: Narrows the recovery path from a general anomaly to one precise question about the defer-cycle guard, with its two independent sourced mechanisms and the two premises that must be resolved before any obligation.

question.question: Does the TryPreAccept recovery path's defer-cycle guard ever fire, and if it cannot, can a recovering coordinator stay deferred instead of restarting phase 1 for the instance?
question.importance: Recovery liveness for an undecided instance: if the guard that is meant to break a defer cycle never executes, a recovering coordinator may keep deferring an instance it cannot own, so that instance (and any client proposal or dependent instance behind it) never reaches a decision. This is a progress concern, not a claim that an already-decided value is unsafe.
participants: recovering coordinator (LeaderId of the instance being recovered)
contexts: recovery of a stalled instance after a slow quorum of Prepare replies that are pre-accepted but conflicting
single recovering coordinator per instance attempt; acceptors may be shared across recovering instances
event_paths: handleTryPreAcceptReply -> notInQuorum guard -> updateDeferred (defer) or startPhase1 (abandon)

supporting_behavior_ids.B-RECOVERY-START: establishes the recovery ballot and the lb whose possibleQuorum is degenerate for this instance
supporting_behavior_ids.B-PREPARE-REPLY-LEADER: is the only path that selects sub-case 4 and therefore the only enabler of the TryPreAccept exchange
supporting_behavior_ids.B-EXEC: triggers recovery after the commit grace period and is where a permanently deferred instance would remain unexecuted

counterevidence: lb.possibleQuorum is only ever assigned false (handleTryPreAcceptReply) and is initialized all-false; even with a corrected loop index the notInQuorum count would be degenerate, so the guard may be inert for two independent reasons.
If handlePrepareReply never selects sub-case 4 because its predicate duplicates sub-case 3, handleTryPreAcceptReply is unreachable and the inert guard has no observable effect.
unknowns: Whether any legal history reaches handlePrepareReply sub-case 4 (TryPreAccept), given the duplicate sub-case 3/4 predicate.
Whether a real defer cycle can arise (it requires the TryPreAccept exchange to be reachable).
Whether executeCommands retriggers recovery for a deferred instance, so that a defer is not permanent even if the guard never fires.
question.trigger_rationale: Two independent sourced mechanisms make the notInQuorum guard inert: possibleQuorum is never set true and the loop tests a constant index instead of the loop variable. It is a written protection ('this is to prevent defer cycles') whose named failure mode is a recovery stall, so the premise of whether the protected cycle can occur is worth resolving.
